solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not at all amused, reply angrily dismissing daughter

indicators.note: an angry reply is a jumbled, upset one, so the letters are thrown into a new order
dismissing means one letter is sent away from the word amused

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly unamused snaps back a cross reply, minus their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing daughter' drops D from AMUSED to leave AMUSE; 'angrily' then rearranges AMUSE plus REPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite rejoinder to thanks, used in the same way as the stock reply 'not at all'.

clue.text: Illegal scheme set up to get coats

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: a scam is an illegal scheme or swindle

explanation.surface: A crooked plan is rigged so that someone ends up with coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' in a down light means read upwards: SCAM turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mac is short for mackintosh, a British word for a raincoat.

clue.text: European hypocrisy dismissing new mammal

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland

indicators.note: dismissing means a letter is sent out of the word for hypocrisy

parts.note: cant is insincere, hypocritical talk

explanation.surface: A European shows his hypocrisy by brushing off a new kind of animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing new' removes N from CANT, leaving CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A polecat is a weasel-family carnivore, so it is one example of a mammal.

clue.text: Hazard of university?

parts.note: hazard as a verb means venture a guess; one made by someone with a university education is, jokingly, an educated one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazard' looks like a noun meaning danger; here it is a guess, as in 'hazard a guess', and 'of university' describes the educated person making it.
explanation.definitionFit: An informed estimate based on knowledge is what the phrase means, punningly a guess by a graduate.

clue.text: One mesmerises subjects ultimately leaving in a confused state

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word subjects
a confused state means the letters of leaving are muddled up

explanation.surface: A hypnotist's subjects end up walking out in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the last letter of 'subjects', comes first, then 'in a confused state' rearranges LEAVING into VENGALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali is the hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, now a byword for someone who controls another by mesmeric power.

clue.text: Casanova's city love

parts.note: Rome is a capital city
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: The great seducer has a favourite city he loves.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Casanova is city plus love.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo, after Shakespeare's lover, is a womaniser, just like a Casanova.

clue.text: Measure of a ruler's progress?

parts.note: a ruler here is the measuring stick, marked off in small imperial units, not a monarch making a royal tour

explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests a king on a royal progress; it is the drawing instrument, whose markings step forward a little at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an imperial length unit of about 2.5 cm, the step marked along a ruler, and also a verb for slow movement.

clue.text: Compound charge applied to idiot

indicators.note: applied to means the charge word is attached after the idiot word

parts.note: nit is British slang for a fool
a rate is a fee or charge

explanation.surface: A fool gets landed with a combined fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a chemical salt of nitric acid, an example of a compound.

clue.text: Indecision of the man with one in position

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: in means the letter for one is placed inside the word for position

parts.note: a station is a post or position
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man can't make up his mind while holding his post.
explanation.walkthrough: HE then I inside STATION gives SITATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitation is a pause from uncertainty, the same idea as indecision.

clue.text: Civilisation finds remedy imprisoning Unionist officer

indicators.note: imprisoning means the word for remedy holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: Society finds a fix by locking up a Unionist officer.
explanation.walkthrough: U and LT go inside CURE, after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A culture is the way of life of a society, in the sense a civilisation has one.

clue.text: The charms of West Africa must include Italian cocktails

indicators.note: must include means the word for charms holds the Italian abbreviation inside

parts.note: mojo is a magic charm, a word of West African origin
It is the abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: West African lucky charms are said to contain an Italian ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: IT goes into MOJOS after MOJ.
explanation.definitionFit: A mojito is a Cuban rum drink with mint and lime, a type of cocktail.

clue.text: Policeman chasing Gospel artist

indicators.note: chasing means the policeman word follows behind the Gospel word

parts.note: John is one of the four Gospels
a constable is a police officer

explanation.surface: A bobby pursues a man of the Gospel who paints.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English Romantic landscape painter, so an artist.

clue.text: Earth's revised opinion?

parts.note: the word earth is what you get from a change of the letters of heart, so the clue word is a rearranged heart

explanation.surface: The planet has had a rethink.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: change the letters of HEART and you get EARTH, the clue's own word; 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having changed one's mind on something means holding a revised opinion.

clue.text: Seize dissident factions in church

indicators.note: in means the anagram sits inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: dissident means rebellious, so the letters of factions break ranks and rearrange

explanation.surface: Rebel groups within a church take over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissident' rearranges FACTIONS to ONFISCAT, which goes inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To confiscate is to take possession of property by authority, that is, to seize it.

clue.text: New honesty boxes left in a sneaky way

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the rearranged letters hold another letter
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the following word's letters

explanation.surface: Unattended honesty boxes, where you pay by trust, get pilfered on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges HONESTY to ONTHESY; 'boxes' then puts L inside. 'honesty boxes' reads as one thing, the unstaffed cash box beside a farm stall, but splits as fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the quiet, secretly or furtively, is to do it sneakily.

clue.text: Emphasise a little money in Europe captures carbon

indicators.note: captures means the coin word takes the element symbol inside it

parts.note: a cent is a small coin of the euro
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Stress that a small sum in Europe can buy carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside CENT after A.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to accent a word is to stress or emphasise it.

clue.text: Sort of weather front Dec could set right

indicators.note: set right means the letters are put into their proper order

explanation.surface: Perhaps December could sort out the weather front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set right' rearranges DEC and COULD together.
explanation.definitionFit: An occluded front forms when a cold front overtakes a warm one, so it is a kind of weather front.

clue.text: Edge that projects, initially from different angle

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word from
different means the letters of angle take another form

explanation.surface: A projecting edge seen first from another angle.
explanation.walkthrough: F, the first letter of 'from', then 'different' rearranges ANGLE into LANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flange is a projecting rim used for strength or attachment, an edge that sticks out.

clue.text: Trouble with private English child under one's wing

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
Pte is the abbreviation for the army rank of private

explanation.surface: A private English soldier takes trouble over a young charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An adoptee is a child taken into a family and cared for, hence under the protection of new parents.

clue.text: Almost get wind of a venue for carnival setting

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: to scent something is to get wind of it
Rio de Janeiro hosts a famous carnival

explanation.surface: Nearly sniffing out a place for a carnival backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from SCENT, giving SCEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline or setting of events in a story or plan.

clue.text: Has another look at sentence concerning engineers and adverts

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
ads is short for adverts

explanation.surface: Someone scans a sentence again about engineers and adverts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition takes 'sentence' as its object: one rereads a sentence. RE (Royal Engineers) is a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To reread something is to look over it a second time.

clue.text: Rather alert, possibly grabbing gold eventually

indicators.note: grabbing means the two halves seize the heraldic gold between them

parts.note: would sooner means would rather

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of alert can be arranged another way

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A rather watchful person may eventually grab gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns ALERT into LATER; 'grabbing' puts OR between SOONER and that.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at some time in the future, the same as eventually.

clue.text: Weight when university's given acceptance?

indicators.note: given acceptance means the letter is taken in by the other word

parts.note: once can mean when, as in once you arrive
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Something weighs on you once your university place is confirmed.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes into ONCE after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is an imperial unit of weight, about 28 grams.

clue.text: Starts to eat and drink, getting you nervous

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Beginning to eat and drink makes you jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and on edge, that is, anxious.

clue.text: Worker engaged in heart-to-heart is antagonistic

indicators.note: engaged in means the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A labourer in a heart-to-heart becomes hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'heart is antagonistic'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker or craftsman.

clue.text: Round of applause given to fish expert

indicators.note: given to means the applause word is added after the fish word

parts.note: a dab is a flatfish
a hand, as in give them a big hand, is a round of applause

explanation.surface: A fish gets a big clap for its skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is a British idiom for someone skilled at something, an expert.

clue.text: Positive response by European viewers

indicators.note: by means placed next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: yes is an affirmative answer

explanation.surface: A European replies in the affirmative to the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are the organs one views with, so jokingly the viewers.

clue.text: Annoys son unloading lorry for no reason

parts.note: to needle is to annoy

indicators.note: unloading means the lorry is emptied of its contents, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A son irritates people by unloading a lorry pointlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unloading' empties LORRY to LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlessly means without necessity, that is, for no good cause.
